title: Counting Dots to Measure a Cell

scenes.visual: Title card 'Counting Dots to Measure a Cell' on a cream background, 16:9. Same COLOUR MAP as the first film: cell membrane = BLUE outline; cytoplasm = PALE BLUE fluid; nucleus = PURPLE; endoplasmic reticulum (ER) = GREEN ribbons; mitochondria = GOLD beans; fat drop = PALE CREAM. Grid dots start HOLLOW GREY and turn GOLD when they land on mitochondria. Cell pictures are cartoons labelled 'schematic'. Every number appears only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: Every job needs the team. But how much of a cell is each part? You can't pour a cell into a measuring cup. So how do scientists find out how much of a cell is mitochondria?
scenes.visual: The heart cell floor plan from the first film shrinks to a corner. A measuring cup appears; a cartoon cell tries to pour into it and does not. A question mark over the cup: 'how much is mitochondria?'
scenes.narration: Every job needs the team. But how much of a cell is each part? You can't pour a cell into a measuring cup. So how do scientists find out how much of a cell is mitochondria?

scenes.tts: First, they preserve the cell and cut a very thin slice. A transmission electron microscope sends a beam of electrons through the slice. It shows small organelles that a school microscope cannot. Because the cell was preserved, each picture is a still view, not a living cell.
scenes.visual: The heart muscle cell cartoon (GOLD beans, PURPLE nucleus) freezes, with a small 'preserved' stamp. A thin blade passes through it; one thin slice lifts out. The slice slides under a tall microscope labelled 'transmission electron microscope'; a beam of small dots labelled 'electrons' passes through it. A grey still picture appears showing oval GOLD-outlined mitochondria. Label: 'a preserved slice, not a living cell'.
scenes.narration: First, they preserve the cell and cut a very thin slice. A transmission electron microscope sends a beam of electrons through the slice. It shows small organelles that a school microscope cannot. Because the cell was preserved, each picture is a still view, not a living cell.

scenes.tts: Next comes a simple trick called point counting. Lay an even grid of dots over the picture. Then look at where each dot lands.
scenes.visual: Label 'point counting'. An even square grid of HOLLOW GREY dots drops onto the grey slice picture and settles. A magnifying circle moves across a few dots, showing one on a mitochondrion and one on the fluid around it.
scenes.narration: Next comes a simple trick called point counting. Lay an even grid of dots over the picture. Then look at where each dot lands.

scenes.tts: Dots that land on mitochondria turn gold. One slice gives only a rough guess. Over many fairly chosen pictures, the share of gold dots estimates the share of the cell's volume that mitochondria fill.
scenes.visual: Dots over mitochondria fill GOLD one after another; the rest stay hollow grey. On-screen text: 'gold dots ÷ all dots ≈ estimated share of the cell's volume that is mitochondria (over many fairly chosen pictures)'. A small stack of further slice pictures fans out behind the first.
scenes.narration: Dots that land on mitochondria turn gold. One slice gives only a rough guess. Over many fairly chosen pictures, the share of gold dots estimates the share of the cell's volume that mitochondria fill.

scenes.tts: Try it on a small grid. Count the gold dots, then count all the dots. The share appears on the screen. This toy grid lands inside the real range for heart muscle.
scenes.visual: A small practice grid of 20 dots on a cartoon slice, labelled 'toy grid, schematic'. A counter ticks up the gold dots to 6, then all dots to 20. On-screen: '6 of 20 dots = 30%'. A horizontal band labelled 'heart muscle, 10 kinds of mammals: 22% to 37%' appears below, and a GOLD marker at 30% drops inside the band.
scenes.narration: Try it on a small grid. Count the gold dots, then count all the dots. The share appears on the screen. This toy grid lands inside the real range for heart muscle.

scenes.tts: Real studies used many pictures and many more dots. Look at heart muscle cells from ten kinds of mammals. Mitochondria filled about a fifth to over a third of the cell, depending on the kind of mammal.
scenes.visual: Many slice pictures fan out like cards, each with its own grid. Ten small mammal silhouettes line up (labelled 'schematic'). The band '22% to 37%' fills GOLD from 22 to 37 on a 0 to 100% scale bar.
scenes.narration: Real studies used many pictures and many more dots. Look at heart muscle cells from ten kinds of mammals. Mitochondria filled about a fifth to over a third of the cell, depending on the kind of mammal.

scenes.tts: Now drop the same grid on a white fat cell. Before the dots turn gold, predict. Will its share be bigger or smaller than the heart cell's?
scenes.visual: A slice picture of a white fat cell appears: one huge PALE CREAM fat drop with a thin rim holding a flat PURPLE nucleus and a few small mitochondria. The same grid of HOLLOW GREY dots drops onto it and waits. Card: 'PAUSE AND PREDICT: bigger or smaller than the heart cell's share?'
scenes.narration: Now drop the same grid on a white fat cell. Before the dots turn gold, predict. Will its share be bigger or smaller than the heart cell's?

scenes.visual: The grid holds unlit over the fat cell; a 5-second ring timer empties.

scenes.tts: Much smaller. Almost every dot lands on fat. One team laid a grid of six hundred eighty-two points over pictures of white fat cells from chicken embryos. Fat droplets filled about nine tenths of the cell. Mitochondria filled less than one percent.
scenes.visual: Nearly every dot lands on the CREAM drop and turns CREAM; only a few dots in the thin rim turn GOLD. On-screen: 'fat droplets together: about 90.9%' and 'mitochondria: about 0.7%'. A small label: 'white fat cells, chicken embryos; grid of 682 points'. The 0 to 100% scale bar now shows a thin GOLD sliver near zero beside the heart band.
scenes.caption: Much smaller. Almost every dot lands on fat. One team laid a grid of 682 points over pictures of white fat cells from chicken embryos. Fat droplets filled about nine tenths of the cell. Mitochondria filled less than one percent.
scenes.narration: Much smaller. Almost every dot lands on fat. One team laid a grid of 682 points over pictures of white fat cells from chicken embryos. Fat droplets filled about nine tenths of the cell. Mitochondria filled less than one percent.

scenes.tts: The fat takes most of the floor. Everything else, mitochondria included, sits in a thin rim around it. Is that rim short of mitochondria? The lesson lets you work it out.
scenes.visual: The fat cell turns into the floor plan from the first film: one CREAM room fills most of the floor; PURPLE, GREEN and GOLD rooms sit in a narrow strip along the walls. A zoom on the strip shows several GOLD beans inside it, with a question mark: 'short of mitochondria?'
scenes.narration: The fat takes most of the floor. Everything else, mitochondria included, sits in a thin rim around it. Is that rim short of mitochondria? The lesson lets you work it out.

scenes.tts: So in the heart cell, mitochondria fill a large share. In the fat cell, stored fat fills most of the space. Many of the same parts, different floor plans.
scenes.visual: Heart floor plan (GOLD room about a third, striped 'muscle fibres' region) and fat floor plan (large CREAM room) side by side, labelled 'drawn the same size, not to real scale'. Labels under them: 'job: work without a break' and 'job: store fat'.
scenes.narration: So in the heart cell, mitochondria fill a large share. In the fat cell, stored fat fills most of the space. Many of the same parts, different floor plans.

scenes.tts: One caution. These cells came from different animals and different studies. They show a pattern across cells with different jobs. They do not prove what causes it.
scenes.visual: Two small source cards appear beneath the floor plans: 'heart: ten kinds of mammals' and 'fat: chicken embryos'. A sign reads 'pattern, not proof'.
scenes.narration: One caution. These cells came from different animals and different studies. They show a pattern across cells with different jobs. They do not prove what causes it.

scenes.tts: Still, simple counting, repeated over many pictures, turned images into numbers. Those numbers show a pattern: cells with different jobs have different floor plans.
scenes.visual: Stacks of slice pictures with grids flip past; gold dots fly out of them and land as tallies that turn into the two floor plans. The heart and fat cell cartoons from the first film's opening return side by side.
scenes.narration: Still, simple counting, repeated over many pictures, turned images into numbers. Those numbers show a pattern: cells with different jobs have different floor plans.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot holding a grid of dots, a few of them gold. Line: 'Counting dots over many slices estimates how much space each part fills.'
